title: The LATEST audit-verdict row per acceptance criterion is authoritative; earlier rows are audit history, not competing claims
decision: Record explicitly that `audit_record` is APPEND-ONLY and that, where an acceptance criterion carries more than one audit-verdict row, the highest-numbered (most recent) row is the authoritative verdict and every earlier row is retained deliberately as audit history. No earlier row is to be deleted, rewritten, or back-filled to match the current verdict. Consequently, any count that sums audit-verdict ROWS rather than criteria overstates the population: at the time of this decision the package holds 95 verdict rows for 86 criteria, and the 9 extras are supersessions, not disagreements — AC-078 and AC-080 carry three rows each, AC-077, AC-079, AC-083, AC-084 and AC-085 carry two.
rationale: Surfaced by a read-only integrity audit on 2026-08-05, which found seven criteria simultaneously holding a Pending row AND a later Met or Partial row with nothing in the schema marking which governs. The audit-verdict schema has no superseded_by or retired_at column, so the ordering rule cannot be expressed structurally and must be written down or it stays an unstated convention that each reader re-derives. Append-only is the RIGHT behaviour for an audit trail and is not being treated as a defect: it preserves how a verdict evolved, which is exactly what an auditor needs — AC-078 legibly moving Pending to Partial to Met as evidence accumulated is more trustworthy than a single row silently rewritten three times. The defect was only that the reading rule was undocumented. IMPORTANT CONSEQUENCE for anyone reading gate_run: its audit_evidence split counts ROWS, not criteria — verified, since evidenced 83 + narrated 12 equals the 95 total exactly — so the headline 'narrated 12' OVERSTATES the honesty gap. Seven of those twelve are superseded Pending rows already replaced by evidenced verdicts; only five are current (AV-004, AV-075, AV-076, AV-081, AV-082) and all five are Pending, i.e. honestly not-yet-assessed. Critically, ZERO Met or Partial verdicts lack evidence, so the C7 concern that a narrated verdict is the graded party grading itself does not presently apply to any passing verdict. Deliberately NOT remedied by mutating rows: giving the stale Pending rows evidence, or rewriting them to match the current verdict, would move the metric without changing the truth, which is the failure mode this package exists to prevent.

title: Arabic term for "Architecture" is الهيكلة — whole term family, noun-in-إضافة, definiteness preserved
decision: Rename the Arabic term for "Architecture" from الهندسة المعمارية to الهيكلة across the product, the 15 affected .dc.html design references, backend notification copy, and all asserting tests. EN keeps "Architecture" — EN/AR diverge semantically by design.
rationale: Operator decision taken on a real production login: الهندسة المعمارية reads as civil/building architecture in Arabic; الهيكلة carries the intended system-structuring sense. Scoped to the whole TERM FAMILY (معمار* in every inflection, plus standalone الهندسة), not the literal phrase, because ar.json was already inconsistent (app.committee = لجنة الهندسة المعمارية vs meetings.mom.committee = لجنة الهندسة) and a literal-only replace would have deepened that split rather than closing it. GRAMMAR: an Arabic adjective phrase (noun + agreeing adjective) becomes a genitive construct (إضافة), which requires dropping ال from the head noun — so this is a rule-based transformation, not a string substitution. DEVIATION FROM THE APPROVED PLAN: the plan collapsed both الثابت المعماري and ثابت معماري onto the definite ثابت الهيكلة; that was written without inspecting the .dc.html prose and produces ungrammatical Arabic in two shapes — after كل (لكل قرار الهيكلة: كل requires an indefinite, and قرار الهيكلة is already an إضافة) and with a trailing indefinite adjective (بثابت الهيكلة قائم, سجل قرار الهيكلة مقترح — قائم/مقترح no longer agree with a now-definite head). Definiteness is therefore PRESERVED: definite source takes الهيكلة, indefinite source takes bare هيكلة. This reproduces every example the operator approved (الهيكلة · ثوابت الهيكلة · سجل قرارات الهيكلة — all definite sources) and fixes both defects. NOT TOUCHED: مهندس/المهندسون/للمهندسين ("engineers" — same root, different word), the عمارة↔معماري word-breaker comment in DecisionSearchProvider.cs (documents SQL Server behaviour, not product copy), and docs/ + tamheed-package/ + .claude/memory/ + handoff/ (records of what happened; renaming them would falsify the record). No data migration: no HasData, no runtime seeder, zero Arabic in 96 EF migrations. VERIFIED: assert-ZERO gate over git-tracked files (not a count — git grep -c counts lines, and ar.json:2 holds two occurrences on one line); rules proven idempotent, so no rule's output can be re-matched by a later rule.

title: In-app user management: Administrator AND Secretary invite users and assign roles from ACMP — supersedes DEC-033 and deviates from the design's read-only-roles note
decision: Build in-app user management. Administrator and Secretary may both (a) INVITE a user — email + full name only, per the design's §(8) USER DETAIL + INVITE — which provisions the Keycloak account and surfaces a temporary password SHOWN ONCE on screen, and (b) ASSIGN ROLES from the app. Four guards are mandatory: nobody may change their own roles; granting Administrator or Chairman is a separate explicitly-confirmed step; the committee may never be left with zero Administrators; every change writes an attributed hash-chained audit event. Any role change FORCES SIGN-OUT so it takes effect immediately rather than at token expiry. ONE ADR covers this, DEC-037's guest invite, and where guest expiry is stored — same client, same credential, same audit path. ADR + FR + AC before any code.
rationale: Operator feature request and interview, 2026-08-11. THE DESIGN ALREADY SPECIFIES MOST OF IT and was found before planning: ACMP Administration.dc.html §(8) fixes the two invite fields (email, full name), the primary action, and — decisively — a status vocabulary that ALREADY CONTAINS `invited` (uStatus: active/invited/disabled). That means the roster was ALWAYS meant to show people who have not signed in yet, so DEF-038 is not a new idea but an unbuilt part of the design. ⚠ DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE REFERENCE, recorded rather than silent (INV-014): the design note reads 'An invitation provisions the account in Keycloak; the role is assigned there and synced read-only.' The operator has decided roles are assigned IN THE APP. That note was doing real security work — an app that cannot write roles cannot escalate privilege, so the design removed that risk BY CONSTRUCTION. The four guards replace it. SUPERSEDES DEC-033: its premise was a Keycloak admin READ to discover invited-but-never-signed-in accounts. Once the app CREATES the accounts it owns the invite record, so the roster's `invited` rows come from ACMP's own data and the read dependency disappears. Known gap accepted: accounts created directly in Keycloak — including the 26 existing production members — remain invisible until first login. CREDENTIAL DELIVERY is a temporary password shown ONCE on screen, because 'no email in v1' is a hard constraint while the design's button says 'Send invitation'; it must never be stored, logged or written to a file — the make-roster-passwords.sh CSV of 26 temp passwords is exactly the hazard this must not repeat. ⚠ RESIDUAL RISK, RAISED ONCE AND ACCEPTED BY THE OPERATOR, recorded so it stays reviewable rather than re-argued: with the Secretary able to both invite AND assign, ONE PERSON can go from nothing to a working privileged account alone. Guard 1 blocks self-escalation but not granting Administrator to a second account they created; guard 2 is a speed bump; GUARD 4 IS THE ACTUAL CONTROL AND IT IS DETECTION, NOT PREVENTION — the same shape the operator accepted in DEC-035. Revisit via a superseding ADR if a reviewer objects; never narrow it silently. ARCHITECTURE NOTE for the ADR: creating a Keycloak user AND a local member row is a distributed write, and DEF-029 means a member row can never be deleted, so a failed second write orphans permanently. Prefer writing Keycloak + a lightweight invite record and leaving ProvisionCurrentUser (ADR-0004, JIT from claims) to create the member row on first login unchanged — one creation path, ADR-0004 intact. The service account must be scoped to manage-users plus role-mapping, NEVER realm-admin, with a file-backed secret per ADR-0032.

title: UAT's database is NEVER reset; the e2e suite stays hardened against accumulated data
decision: UAT keeps its accumulated history. The Playwright suite is not given a clean database before runs; instead it remains hardened so that every spec locates its own fixtures and asserts nothing that depends on being the only rows present. This is the standing policy for any future spec.
rationale: Operator decision, 2026-08-11, taken after DEF-045. A hardened suite passes on ANY database — at 75 topics or 7,500 — whereas resetting only restarts the ratchet and RESTORES THE BLIND SPOT that hid six failures for months. The blind spot is structural, not incidental: CI rebuilds its database every run, so it cannot see this class of defect at all, and a reset-before-run UAT would have exactly the same hole. Keeping UAT accumulated is also the only way it resembles a long-lived production system, which is the specific thing UAT exists to test. REJECTED: reset-before-each-run (fast and predictable, but makes UAT stop resembling production and re-hides the class); and cleaning up the DEF-029 orphan member rows (cosmetic only — DEF-029 means they can be disabled but never deleted, and the hardened lookup no longer cares how many rows exist). CONSEQUENCE ACCEPTED: UAT will keep growing, so any NEW spec must be written page-aware and count-agnostic from the start; the four shapes to avoid are recorded in DEF-045 — non-unique identity lookups, unfiltered paginated lists, absolute counts of anything the environment can add to, and reliance on an e2e-only environment override without a keyed skip.

title: Operator disposition of the four open items after FR-159: OQ-069 (Users moves out of Administration), OQ-071 (split the grant proof), DEF-050 (verify SSM, then fix per ADR-0032), DW-025 (guest windows follow the meeting)
decision: Four answers taken 2026-08-12 by interview, after FR-159 closed. (1) OQ-069 - THE USERS SURFACE MOVES OUT OF ADMINISTRATION. A new Members area holds the directory, the invite (FR-156) and role assignment (FR-157), reachable by Administrator AND Secretary; the Administration area keeps system health, roles, job monitor, streams and notification settings and stays Administrator-only. The Users tab is REMOVED from Administration rather than duplicated - one surface, one place for authorization to be right. (2) OQ-071 - SPLIT THE OBLIGATION. The minimum-grant proof becomes an automated LOCAL test against the bundled Keycloak, asserting that a narrower grant is REFUSED and that manage-users succeeds, so it re-runs every CI run; UAT keeps a reduced CONNECTIVITY check that the service account reaches Keycloak through the deployed proxy with the SSM-delivered secret. (3) DEF-050 - VERIFY BEFORE FIXING, then fix per ADR-0032: read the DEPLOYED env on prod and UAT to settle whether a real Webex token is actually interpolated (which decides the severity the row could not), then mount the five Webex secrets as compose secrets on api and worker, make gen-secrets write them UNCONDITIONALLY, and drop the environment entries. (4) DW-025 - GUEST WINDOWS FOLLOW THE MEETING, and wider than the row proposed: rescheduling MOVES each guest's window, cancelling CLOSES it, and removing a guest from their slot CLOSES it.
rationale: ON OQ-069, the operator rejected both cheaper readings. Narrowing FR-156/157 to Administrator-only was available and refused: the requirements say 'Administrator or Secretary' and the server already honours it, so the product - not the requirement - was wrong. Per-tab gating inside /admin was also refused because it still puts the Secretary inside the Administration area, which is the exact thing the question flagged (SoD-5, permission-matrix row 27). Moving the surface out is the only option where the capability genuinely leaves that area AND does not exist twice. The cost is accepted: the Administration reference draws a Users tab and the design's nav matrix has no Members area, so this is an INV-014 divergence, recorded as SC-008 rather than made silently. ON OQ-071, the substance of the obligation is that a stub cannot evaluate Keycloak's own authorization - and that substance is satisfiable against the same image and the same realm export locally, where it can run on EVERY CI run instead of once on a box that is stopped when idle. What UAT uniquely adds is deployment topology (the /kc prefix behind nginx, the SSM-delivered secret), which is a connectivity question, so it keeps a connectivity check. A one-off manual proof on a stopped box decays; an automated one does not. ON DEF-050, the row itself admitted an unverified fact - 'exposure is probably nil' was inferred from the .env EXAMPLES while the deployed environment comes from SSM. Verifying first is the difference between fixing a dead artifact and rotating a live credential, and this project has paid for asserting instead of checking before. The fix direction follows ADR-0032 because the ADR is explicit and the alternative (accepting environment delivery) would need its own deviation record for a Phase-2 integration that is currently off. ⚠ THE FIX HAS A TRAP THE OPERATOR WAS SHOWN: a compose secrets: entry whose file is missing fails the WHOLE STACK, and gen-secrets only writes the Webex files when WEBEX_ENABLED=true - so the writes must become unconditional, exactly the treatment KeycloakAdmin__ClientSecret got in DW-024. ON DW-025, the operator overruled the deferral AND widened it. The reasoning that made deferral defensible was that the failure mode is inconvenience rather than exposure - but that is only true of RESCHEDULE. Cancelling a meeting leaves an external person holding live access to unpublished material for a meeting that will not happen, and un-assigning a guest from their slot leaves access to a topic they are no longer presenting; both are exposure, not inconvenience. Once the write path exists for one caller, the other two are the same call.

The control is specified in permission-role-matrix section E.1, is registered in DI, is unit-tested, and appears in NO POLICY - so it is never evaluated and FAILS OPEN. The operator undertook to supply them and has not yet; I will not invent a taxonomy for a governance system, and seeding streams while leaving members unassigned is the same outage in slower motion. (2) AC-009 vs AC-034 - AC-034 WINS, AND THE CODE ALREADY AGREES. The two approved ACs contradict each other: ownership is granted ON Accept, so an Owner exists only post-Accept, and AC-034 says only the Secretary may edit after Acceptance while AC-009 says the Owner's edit is accepted. The operator chose the conservative reading - once Accepted, a topic is committee property and its content is locked; the Owner keeps their other capabilities but not editing. NO CODE CHANGES: AC-009 is narrowed to its refusal clause (recorded as SC-009), which #253 already proved live. (3) DEF-056 - ADD AN IAuthorizationMiddlewareResultHandler that emits the audit event when the policy layer forbids. One seam covering every endpoint including ones added later - the same deny-by-default reasoning DEF-052 used, because an opt-in list silently exempts whatever route is added next. ⚠ Two implementation constraints established with the advisor: recover the failing policy name from policy.Requirements (CapabilityRequirement carries PolicyName - confirm there is exactly one and not a merged set), and emit ONLY on authorizeResult.Forbidden, never on Challenged (the 401 path, already covered) and never on success. Resolve the sink from context.RequestServices. Rejected: amending AC-006 to drop the audit clause, on the grounds that 'who tried to mutate governance data and was refused' is precisely the question an architecture committee's log gets asked. (4) AC-011 - TURN KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_ENABLED ON IN CI's E2E STACK. This does far more than unblock one AC: the entire ADR-0038 write path (invite, role assignment, forced sign-out, guest disable) is registered only when the flag is on, so today CI runs seven services with a real Keycloak and never constructs IIdentityProvider at all - the path is reachable only by the manual UAT probe. ✓ VERIFIED BEFORE COMMITTING TO IT: deploy/docker-compose.yml (the dev/e2e compose, not the cloud one) already mounts KeycloakAdmin__ClientSecret into keycloak-config, api and worker at lines 163/183/338 and declares the secret file at 433, so ValidateOnStart will not stop the hosts and a missing secrets file will not fail the stack. Remaining choice at implementation time: set the flag in e2e.yml's env (CI only) or in deploy/.env.example (which changes dev too) - prefer the narrower unless dev should match.
